item.description: European regulators are questioning Binance over its use of a narrow legal exemption to keep serving EU customers without a licence, the Financial Times reported. Binance told Euronews it is working towards authorisation, while ESMA said enforcement is a matter for national authorities.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: France increases defense budget despite strained public finances
item.description: The boost is in line with a new military planning law adopted over the summer.

item.title: Euronews: Can Europe afford its defence boost? MEPs debate in The Ring
item.description: As security and hybrid threats are on the rise across Europe and the war in Ukraine enters its fifth year, the focus in Brussels is firmly on increasing defence spending. But who should pay, and how?

item.title: Euronews: Portugal records biggest EU rise in house prices in second quarter
item.description: Eurostat data shows Portugal recorded the EU's sharpest rise in house prices in Q2 2026 versus a year earlier. In September, national housing costs hit a fresh record high.

item.title: Euronews: Gaza documentary ‘NAZA’ beating ‘Avengers Endgame: Encore’ at box office
item.description: 'NAZA', the award-winning documentary which examines "the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians", is currently beating the recently re-released Marvel film ‘Avengers Endgame: Encore’ at the Italian box office. The documentary is set to be released globally this month.

item.title: Euronews: House prices in Portugal hit new record high in September
item.description: House prices rose 7.9% in September year on year, according to idealista. Portugal recorded the EU’s second‑largest housing price jump in Q2, Eurostat says.

item.title: Euronews: Barcelona-Amsterdam: Europe's most stressful air route for nervous flyers
item.description: The route between Barcelona El Prat and Amsterdam Schiphol tops a ranking that also lists Madrid-London Heathrow in 10th place, according to AirAdvisor.

item.title: Euronews: Falling numbers: Thymaina's plunging population shows Greece's demographic decline
item.description: Desertification in rural areas and on the islands is forcing schools to shut. On a small eastern Aegean island, locals speak of soaring costs, isolation and a future without children.

item.title: Euronews: Rogue AI agents tried and failed to hack US and Canadian government websites
item.description: Researchers cannot confidently say who was responsible, but evidence points to rogue Google and OpenAI agents carrying out a range of aggressive tactics to collect datasets and test their vulnerabilities.

item.title: Euronews: Bradley Whitford receives Hollywood Walk of Fame star
item.description: Bradley Whitford receives the 2,858th star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, celebrating with family and West Wing co-stars in Los Angeles.

item.title: Euronews: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'Digger' – Tom Cruise stuck in postmodernist misfire
item.description: Oscar-winning director Alejandro González Iñárritu teams up with Tom Cruise for 'Digger', one of the boldest and wildest films of 2026. It may also be one of this year's biggest misfires.

item.title: Euronews: Latest news bulletin | October 1st, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 1st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Euronews: Four sailors rescued after sperm whale sinks yacht in South Pacific
item.description: Four sailors were rescued after a sperm whale struck and sank their yacht in the remote South Pacific. A New Zealand Air Force surveillance aircraft helped coordinate the rescue. The crew were taken aboard a cargo ship as their yacht went under.

item.title: Euronews: Death-row inmate Christa Pike seen during murder trial
item.description: File footage shows Christa Pike during her murder trial in Tennessee in 1996 and 2012.

item.title: Euronews: The rise of ‘micro-travel’ and other trends set to hit the big time in 2027, according to Hilton
item.description: Next year, travellers will be taking more frequent, but shorter, trips, booking onto 'growth getaways' and prioritising spending time in nature for wellness purposes.

item.title: Euronews: 'They should cast Jack': Danny Boyle names his pick for the next James Bond
item.description: Jack O’Connell’s name has been mentioned as a possible Bond contender during the audition process, but has not been elevated to frontrunner status like Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, Jacob Elordi and Jack Barton. Now, ex-Bond director Danny Boyle has named O'Connell as his ideal pick for the new 007.

item.title: Euronews: Trump announces $200bn in South Korean energy investment plans
item.description: US President Donald Trump announced Wednesday plans for $200 billion in South Korean investments in US energy projects, including $54 billion for a long-planned liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Alaska that Seoul said it had not yet agreed to invest in.

item.title: Euronews: Greece urges EU to loosen fiscal rules as energy crisis deepens
item.description: High energy prices and military escalation at energy facilities in the Middle East prompted Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis to ask Brussels for greater fiscal flexibility. Greece has the largest debt among EU countries and is heading to polls in 2027.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: Burnham ‘really concerned’ if Man City’s UAE owners sell club after breaking rules
item.description: The U.K. prime minister — and former Greater Manchester mayor — praises the under-fire Premier League club's Emirati ownership as "huge partner" in building up the city.

item.title: Euronews: Several regions of Ukraine hit by power cuts after Russian strikes, grid operator says
item.description: Kyiv said it was Moscow's opening salvo in an expected campaign to try to knock out heating and power as winter approaches.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: Latvia detains couple suspected of spying for Russia
item.description: Authorities allege the pair collected information on NATO forces, military aircraft and Latvia's support for Ukraine.

item.title: Euronews: ‘Thrilling’: Dutch cattle farmers switch to rice as solution to warmer climate and sinking peatlands
item.description: Dutch cattle farming dries out peatland and releases CO2. Is switching to Japanese rice-growing a solution?

item.title: Euronews: Lost in translation: Montenegro's EU accession faces a language barrier
item.description: Montenegro may not be able to accurately translate all EU laws in time for accession, so the European Commission is currently weighing options for a derogation, including allowing Podgorica to use an existing EU language to fill the gaps. Croatian would be the most obvious choice.

item.title: Euronews: PM Netanyahu says Israel warned UK of suspected Iran attack plot on RAF airbase
item.description: After three days of investigations, including using a bomb disposal team, police said on Tuesday they had found no explosives in the vehicles, but they had retrieved a "quantity of petrol."

item.title: Euronews: Oil hovers around $100 as US bonds suffer their worst quarter since 1994
item.description: Oil prices bounced back above $100 a barrel on Thursday as a US-Iran deal remained elusive, while European stocks fell and US government bonds came off their worst quarter since 1994, with the 10-year Treasury yield at its highest since 2007.

item.title: Euronews: France's borrowing rate keeps rising, hitting its highest level since 2002
item.description: The new rise in France's ten-year borrowing rate, now close to 5%, shows investors' mounting distrust of a public debt that keeps climbing.

item.title: Euronews: Is the EU planning to freeze funds to German states that voted for the AfD?
item.description: Claims circulating online allege that the EU is threatening to block funds intended for the German state of Saxony-Anhalt, after the far-right AfD party won a recent election there. However, there's no evidence that this is the case.

item.title: Euronews: Crete at the mercy of severe weather: Floods, landslides, power cuts and closed schools
item.description: Heavy rain and thunderstorms have turned roads into torrents, causing landslides and power cuts, while authorities and civil protection are on high alert.

item.title: Euronews: Russia's jury reform draws fire for handing verdicts back to the state
item.description: The Supreme Court proposals would allow presiding judges to "clarify" questions during deliberations and reduce jury panels from six or eight members to four, changes lawyers say undermine the independence of a system that acquits at 60 times the national average in non-jury trials.

item.title: Euronews: Two million Portuguese suffer from migraine, but many still lack care
item.description: Worldwide, around 1.3 billion people live with migraine, making it one of the most common neurological disorders and a leading cause of disability. Despite its impact, it is underdiagnosed and many patients still lack adequate care.

item.title: Euronews: Eviction: Where are tenants most and least protected across Europe?
item.description: The eviction of a disabled 87-year-old woman in Madrid from a flat she lived in for 70 years has sparked outrage and comparisons of renter rights across the continent.

item.title: Euronews: Gimmick or recipe for success? Japan's convenience stores test AI flavours
item.description: Japanese convenience store chains are turning to AI for dessert ideas. Some are unexpected mashups.

item.title: Euronews: Tallinn Defence EXPO: Counter-drone systems and robot soldiers steal the show
item.description: Drones have changed the face of war in Ukraine. At the Tallinn Defence EXPO, Estonian companies showed the counter-drone systems and battlefield robots they say Europe now needs.

item.title: Euronews: Humanoid robots: China builds them, but Germany could supply the joints and hands
item.description: Europe has so far built few humanoid robots, yet could profit from each one. German car part suppliers may play a key role in joints, says a Fraunhofer study.

item.title: Euronews: Attacker's identity and motive unknown after flydubai flight to Israel escapes disaster after pilot stabbed
item.description: Saudi and UAE authorities have said little publicly beyond confirming that investigations were underway. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said the copilot was arrested.
